sections.content: Evaluation often depends on whether the speaker presents something as certain or questions it. Expressions such as es *evidente* *que* normally take the indicative when the speaker presents the statement as a fact. Expressions such as no *creo* que and es *posible* que normally take the subjunctive when the speaker doubts, questions or presents a possibility.

items.spanish: Es evidente que la noticia ha provocado una reacción inmediata.
items.english: It is clear that the news has caused an immediate reaction.

items.spanish: No creo que la fuente sea completamente fiable.
items.english: I do not think the source is completely reliable.

items.spanish: Es posible que el suceso tenga otra explicación.
items.english: It is possible that the event has another explanation.

items.spanish: Creo que los investigadores necesitan más información.
items.english: I think the investigators need more information.

sections.content: Treat certainty and evaluation carefully: affirmative statements of belief commonly use the indicative, while doubt and possibility commonly trigger the subjunctive.
